title: Back Market Sells 'Excellent' Phones With Greasy Handprints
meta_description: Back Market customer finds greasy handprints on 'excellent condition' phone. Here's what quality grading actually means vs what some companies call it.
content:
Back Market Sells 'Excellent' Phones With Greasy Handprints

A UK customer just posted proof that Back Market sold him a phone with visible greasy handprints. Marketed as 'excellent condition.'

Quote: 'goods in fair condition sold as excellent... can easily see greasy hand marks on the item.'

This isn't about one bad phone. It's about an industry that lies about condition grades because most customers can't return international orders.

What 'Excellent' Actually Means (Industry-Wide Problem)

Most refurbished sellers use grades like marketing terms instead of quality standards. 'Excellent' becomes whatever they need to move inventory at higher margins.

The real problem? No standardization. One company's 'excellent' is another's 'good' is another's 'acceptable.' Customers comparing grades across sites are comparing completely different standards.

Amazon Renewed, Swappa, Gazelle, Back Market — they all define grades differently. Some focus on functionality over cosmetics. Others prioritize appearance but ignore battery health. Most don't even specify what they're grading.

When you're buying sight unseen, grade inflation becomes fraud. Especially when return policies make exchanges expensive or impossible.

How We Actually Grade Devices

Our 65-point inspection isn't marketing copy. It's a literal checklist each device must pass before we assign a grade.

Excellent means zero cosmetic defects visible from 12 inches away, 90%+ battery health, all ports and sensors tested functional. If there's a greasy handprint, it gets cleaned or downgraded. Period.

iPhone 13 Refurbished -- Excellent from $349

Actually excellent condition with 90%+ battery health and zero visible wear from normal viewing distance.

Check availability

Good grade means light wear that doesn't affect function — micro-scratches on the back, minor scuffs on corners, 85%+ battery health. Still very clean, just not perfect.

Fair means obvious wear but fully functional — visible scratches, dents, or discoloration, 80%+ battery health. Honest about what you're getting.

We photograph actual condition, not stock photos. The device in the photo is the device you receive. What a concept.

Why Geographic Distance Enables Grade Fraud

Back Market operates from Europe. Returns mean international shipping, customs delays, weeks without a phone. Most customers just keep whatever arrives rather than deal with the hassle.

That's exactly what these companies count on. Grade inflation works because distance makes returns impractical.

We ship from Tucson. Returns are domestic, prepaid, and processed within 24 hours. If we grade something wrong, you can actually send it back without international shipping nightmares.

Geographic accountability matters in refurbished electronics. You want to buy from someone you can actually reach if there's a problem.

FAQ

Do you ever get grading wrong?

Occasionally, yes. When it happens, we immediately offer replacement, refund, or credit toward a higher grade at no charge. Mistakes happen — how companies handle them matters.

How do you clean devices before selling?

Every device goes through ultrasonic cleaning, alcohol sanitization, and compressed air port cleaning. No exceptions. If we can't clean something completely, it gets noted in the condition description.

What if I disagree with your grading?

Send photos within 30 days. If you're right, we'll refund the grade difference immediately and let you keep the device. We'd rather lose money than lose trust.

Grade inflation is industry-wide fraud enabled by impractical return policies. Want to know what excellent condition actually looks like? Buy from someone in your own country who stakes their reputation on honest grading.
